text:
zoe: heads up — small subset (~5%) of requests keep landing on v1 even after we bumped B to 10% yesterday. not matching rollout dashboard.

devin: do you mean the canary variant? which route?

zoe: api /generate, policy=rollout-affinity, key=user.id_hash, buckets A:90 B:10. dashboard shows 10% for B, but logs show persistent clients stuck on A even after cookie changed.

samir: paste rollout config and a sample request/response headers

zoe: ```json
{
  "policy": "affinity",
  "key": "user_id",
  "buckets": [ { "id": "A", "pct": 90 }, { "id": "B", "pct": 10 } ],
  "assignment_window": 86400,
  "sticky_ttl": 0
}
```

maria: sticky_ttl 0? that means fallback to cookie-based sticky with default domain behavior. could be domain/path mismatch.

devin: nginx proxy adds header X-User: 12345 and Set-Cookie: redwood_assign=A; Domain=.example.com; Path=/; Max-Age=86400

zoe: but clients in subdomain staging.example.com show cookie being set for example.com? i saw requests from staging still carrying cookie for production due to path.

samir: if assignment_window is non-zero the runtime should use server-side assignment ignoring cookie. looks like assignment_window set but sticky_ttl=0 causes runtime to still consult cookie. bug?

rollouts-bot: new rollout event: deploy/rollout 2024-07-15T09:12Z - policy change applied

aj: quick repro: `curl -H "X-User: 1234" -H "Host: staging.example.com" https://staging.gateway/... -v` shows `Set-Cookie: redwood_assign=A; Domain=example.com` which the browser will send back to production hosts too.

infra-bot: routing logs: `2024-07-15T09:18Z user=1234 chosen=A reason=cookie_present` (attached)

maria: probable root cause: cookie normalization uses top-level domain computed by publicsuffix library; for some internal domains publicsuffix returns example.com causing cross-env cookie sharing. propose changing cookie domain to exact host or use subdomain-only cookies for staging.

devin: also double-check hash-salt drift: if user_id hashing used different salt in earlier runtime versions, assignments can flip when runtime rolled. but that would be flip not persistent A for same client.

zoe: proposed short-term: set sticky_ttl to non-zero so server assignment wins. long-term: fix cookie domain computation and runtime precedence docs.

samir: I'll open a quick patch to prefer assignment_window when present and log when cookie/domain mismatch detected. will also add a rollout check in console to flag cookie use.

aj: thx. can someone add an opt-in telemetry metric for "cookie-overrides-assignment" so we can measure impact?

devin: +1

ops-bot: created incident ticket INF-2312, assignees: samir, maria, devin

zoe: thanks all. will monitor. :thumbsup:
